findings.reason: the section must name where the scanner lives and be committed (extending the `scripts/` audit pattern, and citing `tests/physics/test_dependency_contract.py` as the existing declaration-check owner), so the census is reproducible rather than a one-off.
findings.text: the §2 census is a substantial static-import scanner (AST walk over `imas_ambix/`/`tests/`/`scripts/`, module→distribution mapping via `importlib.metadata.packages_distributions`, per-distribution classification) that proposes to "change no other file", yet the repository already carries the precedent for such a scanner — `scripts/circular_assertion_audit.py` walks every `.py` under a tree, parses with `ast`, resolves imports, and ships a companion `.toml` config — and its own done-when declares the artifact durable (an evidence fragment) while the tool that produced it is uncommitted and its home unnamed. A measurement nothing can re-run leaves the census unreviewable and §4's "compare this sync's removal list with the census" resting on a process that no longer exists

findings.reason: the "default" definition must be aligned with the mandated-tooling owner (or §3 must name `pytest-timeout`/`pytest-xdist` in the dev group explicitly), otherwise a plain `uv sync` still does not yield the working stack.
findings.text: §2 defines "default" to include the test runner "and its plugins named in the pytest configuration"; inspected, `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` in `pyproject.toml` names no plugins (`addopts = "-ra --strict-markers"` only), and no module under `imas_ambix/` or `tests/` imports `pytest_timeout` or `pytest_xdist`, while the workstation's binding environment rules (`~/.agents/AGENTS.md`, Test Execution Protocol) require a per-test bound and prefer `pytest-xdist`. Under §2's own rule both plugins classify as *unused*, so the plan would relock the project and still leave the fleet's mandated test tooling undeclared — re-creating the exact debt §1 retires. The environment-policy owner is the document that names what tooling default sessions require; the census rule should extend that owner rather than invent a parallel one from the intrinsic pytest config alone

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan adds no module and abstracts nothing; it edits `pyproject.toml` and relocks, which is correctly thin for a declaration change.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2's "default library" definition duplicates the environment-policy owner and diverges from it: the rule counts only "pytest and its plugins named in the pytest configuration", which names none, so the toolkit the fleet's own rules mandate (`pytest-timeout`, `pytest-xdist`) classifies as unused.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; the plan adds no public definition, CLI option, MCP view or refusal family (one evidence HTML is not a definition family), so nothing needs retiring or merging.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2 proposes a new static import-census scanner without citing the repository's existing AST source-scanning audit (`scripts/circular_assertion_audit.py`) or its existing declaration-contract test (`tests/physics/test_dependency_contract.py`), and leaves the scanner's home undefined.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no wrapper over existing machinery is proposed; §3 edits the owner of the declaration (`pyproject.toml`) directly rather than layering beside it.
